findings.F1: The main measure falls on the side the idea predicts but just short of the bar: the pooled 72-hour slope is +0.000469 with t 1.90 on 2,837 trending grid cases (1,190 with a positive forecast), and the supporting check passes (top third of positive forecasts minus forecast 0 = +0.0098), so the shortfall is about precision, not direction.
findings.F2: The effect is small against the market's own moves and uneven across slices: the 72-hour excess return has a standard deviation of 0.090; per-coin t runs from -0.78 (LTC) to 2.08 (ETH); per-year t runs from -0.78 (2018) to 3.10 (2020); and per-window t ranges from -1.66 to 3.73 with many near zero, so the six default coins alone give too few independent cases to clear t 2.
findings.F3: The plan's forecast throws away part of the signal: within positive forecasts the 72-hour slope is flat (+0.000015, t 0.04, n 1,190), yet the raw volume ratio predicts the 72-hour excess return with t 2.80 (n 2,837), and its quintiles rise in order (-0.0013, -0.0001, +0.0019, +0.0082, +0.0088), so the standardise-and-clip step dilutes a graded effect.
findings.F4: The effect is clearer at a shorter horizon: on a 24-hour grid the forecast slope has t 3.25 (n 8,577), positive in 62.5 % of windows; the high third of positive forecasts earns +0.0045 excess against -0.0005 at forecast 0; and the slope is positive on 5 of 6 coins (ETH t 2.49, XRP t 2.20, ZEC t 1.81), while at 168 and 336 hours t falls to 1.39 and 0.51.
findings.F5: The rising-month condition is not where the effect lives: the price-recomputed volume ratio predicts the 72-hour excess return about as well on non-trending grid cases (slope 0.0062, t 2.91, n 2,305) as the raw ratio does on trending ones (slope 0.0068, t 2.80), and at 24 hours it also holds off-regime (t 2.70, n 7,120).

ideas.name: heavy-volume follow-through, more coins
ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day return is positive, the higher its daily volume relative to its own 20-day average volume, the higher its return over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A rising coin trading on unusually heavy volume is a reason to be long for the next few days, and a rising coin on thin volume is a reason to refuse the trade.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's daily volume relative to its own 20-day average volume, the higher its return over the next 3 days, whether its 30-day return is rising or falling.
ideas.consequence: Unusually heavy volume in a coin is a reason to lean long for the next few days, and unusually thin volume is a reason to refuse a long, in any month.
ideas.name: heavy volume precedes gains

ideas.idea: While a coin's 30-day return is positive, the higher its daily volume relative to its own 20-day average volume, the higher its return over the next 1 day.
